Generic procurement metadata is not a requirement.","suppliedContext":"PRIOR FINDING: old exchange-count cap check and later increment were non-atomic under concurrency.

CUT: the custom LMT solicit/invoke source and tests were deleted after confirming no live consumer references. Package exposes only typed RMN solicitation and signed A2A execution. All 58 JSON exchange records moved byte-for-byte to content/assets/legacy/retired-json-exchanges.4a679555 with ordered path/content digest sha256:4a6795556125fc71cb4ca236a1fea1cdeccefe4d486a3ce1c95e8f32856cfac4. Operational content/exchanges now contains only .gitkeep.

CAPACITY: policy declares maximumConcurrentLots exactly 1. Offer formation reads that policy and refuses if it is not exactly 1. Executor acquires data/nvidia-request-slot.lock using openSync(path, wx); while owned it waits only to a bounded deadline, refuses when timeout expires, reclaims locks older than 180 seconds (longer than the 130-second maximum network subprocess), and removes the lock in finally. Tests prove potential-owner refusal, stale recovery, release, policy drift refusal, and offer maximumConcurrentLots=1.

SINGLE SETTLEMENT: run-one-exchange is stateless and writes no file. execute-rmn-inference validates canonical RMN, runs the adapter under the exclusive slot, forms FOUR completion and WIT transition, then hires RWIL/RDF exactly once. A fresh live market-selected NVIDIA lot under signed law ni:///sha-256;tWSfEdGsqk0rvj-s8ZslGMGZFNZTwnRifjD0gPd0tG4 returned schema-assayed {ready:true}; live content/exchanges remained empty; one RMN object and one RWIL .nq graph appeared; lock absent afterward. Provider verify passes 7/7.

REVIEWER-POOL RESIDUE: source acceptance is already fail-closed: fresh acceptance requires reviews.length>=minimumReviews and acceptedCount>rejectedCount; protected acceptance requires protected witness and acceptedCount>=1. Empty pools cannot accept. completion.text: {"accepted":true,"summary":"The prior non-atomic exchange-count cap/increment concurrency finding is resolved by the combination of: policy hard-capping maximumConcurrentLots=1, OS-atomic openSync wx-flag exclusive acquisition, bounded deadline with refusal on timeout, stale recovery at 180 s (safely above the 130 s maximum subprocess duration), and finally-block lock removal. Data migration of 58 legacy records is clean with a verified byte-for-byte content digest. Test suite covers the five required behavioral paths: active-owner refusal, stale recovery, release, policy-drift refusal, and offer cap enforcement. Two advisory residues remain below critical threshold. The change is materially sound relative to the bounded scope.","findings":[{"severity":"medium","problem":"Stale-lock reclamation race: if two waiters simultaneously observe a lock older than 180 s and both attempt to unlink then re-acquire with wx, the unlink is not atomic with the subsequent open, leaving a narrow window where the second waiter may see ENOENT then succeed with wx, producing a double-acquisition despite the single-slot policy.","evidence":"Context states the executor 'reclaims locks older than 180 seconds' but does not confirm whether reclamation is an atomic rename-over or a separate unlink + openSync(wx) pair. A two-step unlink-then-create sequence has a race window between the unlink and the new wx create; two concurrent stale-detectors can both unlink and both succeed.","recommendation":"Implement stale reclamation atomically: write a tempfile then rename it over the lock path (POSIX atomic replace), or after a detected-stale unlink catch a subsequent EEXIST from wx as a lost race and abort rather than retry, ensuring exactly one waiter acquires the reclaimed slot."},{"severity":"low","problem":"Process-crash lock persistence bypasses the finally block: a SIGKILL or OOM termination of the owner prevents lock removal, leaving the slot blocked for up to 180 s regardless of actual work completion.","evidence":"Lock removal is in a finally block, which is skipped on unhandled signal or OOM kill. The 180 s stale threshold exceeds the 130 s maximum network subprocess, so a crashed owner causes a minimum 180 s slot blackout with no active alerting path described.","recommendation":"Document the 180 s recovery window as an explicit operational SLA. Add a monitoring hook or log emission when stale reclamation fires so that operations can detect crash loops before they compound into extended unavailability."},{"severity":"low","problem":"Reviewer-pool minimum threshold allows a zero-review bypass if minimumReviews is misconfigured to 0: reviews.length >= minimumReviews evaluates true on an empty array, potentially satisfying the length guard without any actual review present.","evidence":"Context states 'empty pools cannot accept' and the guard is reviews.length >= minimumReviews && acceptedCount > rejectedCount. If minimumReviews=0 the length condition is trivially satisfied. Whether a separate hard floor of 1 exists independent of the configured value is not confirmed in the supplied context.","recommendation":"Add an invariant assert or runtime guard that minimumReviews >= 1 at policy load time, so a misconfigured zero value is rejected at configuration rather than silently enabling bypass of the acceptance threshold."}]}
